evidence.quote: Here, the route passes through three tunnels and a narrow canyon, snaking along the foot of sharp cliffs and a boulder-strewn creek.

evidence.claim: Known as the Maricopa Highway, it was intended to carry commerce and tourism between the San Joaquin Valley and southern California.
evidence.quote: Originally, it was known as the Maricopa Highway, and it was to be the great connection for commerce and tourism between the San Joaquin Valley and southern California.

evidence.claim: The Forest Service now identifies it as especially popular with motorcyclists.
evidence.quote: The route is especially popular with motorcyclists, both individuals and clubs.

evidence.claim: Bellyache Springs has two naming legends.
evidence.quote: Bellyache Springs - Legend has it that the springs here received this name because early travelers were so thirsty by the time they got there that they over drank and got bellyaches. One Forest Service legend is that early rangers met here on horse back to discuss, or belly-ache about Forest Service issues.

evidence.claim: One tells of thirsty travelers who drank too much when they reached the springs and suffered for it.
evidence.quote: Legend has it that the springs here received this name because early travelers were so thirsty by the time they got there that they over drank and got bellyaches.

evidence.claim: A Forest Service legend instead has early rangers gathering on horseback to complain about their work.

evidence.claim: Wheeler Blumberg found hot sulphur springs here in 1890 after following a deer he had shot into a ravine.
evidence.quote: Blumberg discovered the hot springs here in 1890 when he was out on a hunting trip. He shot a deer which fell into a ravine. When Blumberg climbed into the canyon, he discovered hot sulphur springs and cold mountain water springs.

evidence.claim: He opened a resort the next year with 14 rental cabins and a swimming pool.
evidence.quote: The founder of the resort, Wheeler Blumberg, established the resort in 1891. It had 14 rental cabins, a swimming pool, bar, and more.

evidence.claim: The resort closed in 1997.
evidence.quote: The resort operated throughout the 1900s, but closed in 1997.

evidence.claim: The road’s engineering gives another measure of the canyon: three tunnels and three bridges were needed to build the Maricopa Highway through Wheeler Gorge.
evidence.quote: The canyon is so narrow that three tunnels and an additional three bridges had to be constructed for Maricopa Highway to be built.
